reports.title: Tango Therapeutics Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

desk.headline: Net loss of $68.4m ($0.39 a share), wider than estimates; $977.5m cash; Phase 3 pancreatic cancer study planned for 1H 2027

other.label: Net loss
other.change: vs net income of $15.9m a year ago

results: Tango is a clinical-stage cancer drug developer with no product sales; it had no revenue this quarter, against $53.8m of one-off collaboration revenue from Gilead a year ago.
The net loss was $68.4m, or $0.39 a share, versus a profit of $15.9m a year earlier.
Research spending rose 59% to $48.9m as the vopimetostat and TNG456 trials advanced; admin costs more than tripled to $29.2m, partly from changes to equity awards for former executives.
Cash and investments stood at $977.5m at 30 September, up from $343.1m at the end of 2025, which the company expects to fund its current operating plan.
At ESMO in October, vopimetostat plus Revolution Medicines' daraxonrasib showed an 82% response rate in previously treated pancreatic cancer patients.

guidance.summary: No financial guidance and no specific cash runway date; the company says its cash funds its current operating plan. Pipeline timelines: lung cancer data for vopimetostat and TNG456 in January 2027, and two pancreatic cancer studies, including a Phase 3, to start in the first half of 2027.

points: The CEO said the ESMO data reinforced the program's potential in MTAP-deleted, RAS-mutant pancreatic cancer.
Tango has discussed its front-line Phase 3 plan with the FDA and aims to start the study in the first half of 2027.
It plans to ask regulators about a possible accelerated approval path in second-line pancreatic cancer.
Its lung cancer strategy, backed by vopimetostat and TNG456 data, is due in January 2027.
Research has been refocused on PRMT5-targeted drugs.
call.source: CEO comments in the results release (Exhibit 99.1); no call coverage found

watch: January 2027 lung cancer data for vopimetostat and TNG456.
Start of the front-line Phase 3 pancreatic cancer study and supply of daraxonrasib for it.
Feedback from regulators on a possible accelerated approval in second-line pancreatic cancer.
